one_month_reasoning: Window 2026-10-06 to 2026-11-04 contains Vicor's Q3 2026 report (expected ~Oct 20-21, matching the Apr 21 and Jul 21 report dates), plus Q3 hyperscaler capex results in late October and Form 144 insider-sale notices filed Oct 1-2. The Q3 number itself is already pre-announced (revenue >30% sequential, i.e. >$186M vs $143.4M), so the surprise will be in (a) how much of the Q3 royalty step-up is catch-up versus run-rate, (b) Q4 guidance and product gross margin, and (c) whether more VPD licensees sign. The stock just rose ~62% in five weeks (from $188.55 on 2026-09-04 to $305.61), and insiders keep selling, so short-horizon reversal and 'sell the pre-announced news' risk tilt the centre slightly below spot; but a further licence announcement could add 15-20% in a day (as on Sept 16 and Sept 22). I therefore centre the 1-month distribution at ~$300 (about 2% below spot) with monthly vol 27% (95%/3.5), roughly symmetric.

fair_value.method: 50/50 blend of (1) SOTP P/E on CY2028 (NTM at the horizon) recurring earnings: product EPS $4.03 x 27.6x peer median + recurring royalty EPS $3.02 x 15x + $13 net cash = $170, and (2) a 5-year FCF DCF (WACC 10.5%, terminal growth 4%) = $181. One-off licence catch-ups, fixed-term licence payments and the Q2 option-exercise tax benefit are excluded from the earnings capitalised.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: SOTP on CY2028E: product pre-tax $253M (rev $900M x 52% GM - $240M opex + $25M interest) -> $4.03/sh x 27.6x; recurring royalties pre-tax $190M (royalties $220M - $30M IP/legal costs) -> $3.02/sh x 15x; tax 22%; 49M diluted shares; net cash ~$650M = $13.3/sh; remaining fixed licence payments ~$0.2/sh. Total ~$170.

inputs_detail.derivation: 2026E product ~ $471M (Q1 $98M = $113.0M less $15.0M royalty; Q2 $112.9M; Q3/Q4 ~$125M/$135M on management's 'double-digit sequential' advanced-product growth). 2027E $700M (+49%) supported by $379.7M one-year backlog (+145% y/y) and book-to-bill >1; 2028E $900M (+29%) slowing toward the capex file's base case of 2028 customer AI capex only +22% over 2027. Fab 1 output target of a $1.5B run-rate means capacity does not bind before 2028.

Q2 2026 total GM 58.0% on $143.4M with $30.4M royalties at ~100% margin implies product GM ~46.7% ($52.7M/$112.9M), depressed by one-time equipment relocation; management guides margin expansion with volume. 52% assumes partial recovery, well short of the 70% long-term company target which includes royalties.
Q2 2026 opex = $83.1M GP - $34.9M operating income = $48.2M/qtr (~$193M/yr); grown ~18%/yr for headcount, second fab start-up and continued ITC litigation.

Legacy recurring royalties ~ $15M/qtr (Q2 2026 royalty $30.4M less $15M from the new fixed-payment licence). Four VPD licensees now; the Sept 16 non-exclusive licence lifted Q3 guidance by ~20 points of revenue (~$29M), part of which is assumed catch-up. Run-rate from new VPD licences assumed ~$35-40M/qtr by 2028; existing licences expire in 2027 and must be renegotiated (risk).

inputs_detail.value: Fixed-term licence $60M ($5M x4 then $10M x4; $10M of Q2's $15M was accounting catch-up); Q2 2026 tax benefit $10.9M (-27.9% ETR from option exercises); Q2 2025 $45M patent-litigation settlement; Q1 2026 $28.6M litigation payment
inputs_detail.derivation: Q2 2026 reported EPS $1.04; ex the $10M catch-up and the $10.9M tax benefit at a normal 22% rate, recurring Q2 EPS ~ ($34.9M - $10M + $4.0M) x 0.78 / 47.7M = ~$0.47.

Peer median forward P/E of 11 AI-power/AI-hardware/power-semi peers (range 15.2x-56.0x). No premium: VICR's 2028 product growth (~29%) is below peers' next-year EPS growth median (~53%), customer concentration is high, and VICR's own history shows three failed re-ratings (2018, 2021, 2023).

Discount to peer median because licences are finite (current agreements expire 2027), depend on the second ITC case (final determination 2027) and are lumpy; roughly the low end of the peer range (NVDA 15.2x).
Q2 2026 cash $453.6M, no debt; plus ~$350M operating cash over 12 months less ~$150M capex for Fab 2/3 site purchases and fit-out (H1 2026 capex $23.6M).
Q2 2026 diluted 47.7M; 46.1M basic (34.39M common + 11.72M Class B at 2026-07-22); +~1.3M/yr from option exercises.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: FCF CY2028-31: $280M, $378M, $510M, $640M on revenue $1.12B/$1.40B/$1.70B/$2.0B and FCF margins 25%/27%/30%/32%; WACC 10.5%; terminal growth 4% (TV $10.2B); valued at end-2027 => EV ~$8.24B + net cash $0.65B = $8.89B / 49M sh = $181.

inputs_detail.derivation: 2029 matches the Simply Wall St consensus ($1.4B); 2027 consensus $969M; path stays below management's $2.5B target, which needs a second fab with phased build-out from late 2027/2028.
Consensus 2029 net margin ~32%; FCF held below net margin in 2028-29 for Fab 2/3 capex.
High-beta small-cap semi: realized vol 95%, three >50% drawdowns since 2018; Kalshi prices 21% odds of a 2027 US recession; equity-only financing.
AI data-center capex growth decelerates from +50% (2027 base) to +22% (2028 base) in the capex file; long-run growth set modestly above nominal GDP.

bear.story: The base-rate path: like 2018 (-51% in 12 months after the peak), 2021-22 (-68%) and 2023-24 (-54%). Royalty step-up proves largely catch-up, licences up for renewal in 2027 reprice lower, product margins stay in the 40s and AI capex digests in 2027-28 (Kalshi 21% 2027 recession). Market pays ~25x a ~$5 recurring EPS, plus cash.

base.story: Product revenue ~ $700M in 2027 and VPD royalties stay at a ~$35M/qtr run-rate; consensus 2027 EPS ~$6 is roughly met but royalties are valued below product earnings, and the multiple compresses from 48x toward ~38x forward as growth slows. The stock ends a little below today.

bull.story: VPD licensing becomes an industry tax on AI accelerator power delivery (more hyperscaler and OEM licensees, ITC exclusion in 2027 forces stragglers), 2nd-gen VPD ramps in late Q3/Q4 2027, and 2028 EPS heads to $10+; the market pays ~45x like ALAB/MPWR.

comps_summary.peer_range: Forward P/E 15.2x (NVDA) to 56.0x (ALAB); proxy forward EV/EBITDA 10.8x (POWI) to 67.7x (ALAB). All are finviz next-fiscal-year (~CY2027) P/E at 2026-10-05 close. Forward EV/EBITDA is a proxy, trailing EV/EBITDA x (forward P/E / trailing P/E), i.e. it assumes EBITDA grows in line with EPS. Fiscal years are not calendar-aligned for NVDA, MRVL, AVGO, CRDO and ADI, so the comparison is within about 2 quarters.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: VICR trades at 48.1x its next-year consensus EPS ($6.35), which includes royalties, against a peer median of 27.6x. We apply 27.6x (the median) to product earnings and 15x (bottom of the range) to recurring royalty earnings. The blended ~21x on CY2028 recurring EPS, or ~25x on CY2027 recurring EPS of ~$5.0, sits inside the peer range in its lower half.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: We apply no premium. VICR's product growth (2028E ~29%) is below the peer next-year EPS growth median (~53%). Its product gross margin (~47% in Q2 2026) is below MPWR or ALAB. Its customers are concentrated: the 10-K says most Advanced Products revenue comes from one or a few customers. Its own history argues against a durable re-rating: three prior AI or data-center re-ratings each gave back 50-68% within about 12 months. The royalty stream gets a discount because current licences expire in 2027 and depend on an ITC final determination in 2027, and because about two-thirds of Q2's new-licence revenue was accounting catch-up. The sell-side mean target of about $387-394 is not used as a justification.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$145, VICR would sit under ~25x CY2027 recurring EPS less cash, and back at its April 2026 breakout level before the Q1 backlog surge. That would most likely mean a fundamental break: VPD royalty payments disputed or renegotiated down at the 2027 renewals, the ITC case going against Vicor, or AI product orders being cut (backlog falling below the $300M Q1 level). Ordinary 95% volatility would not by itself explain it.

reasoning: Facts: Q2 2026 revenue was $143.4M ($112.9M product, $30.4M royalty) and diluted EPS $1.04. That EPS is flattered by $10M of licence catch-up (the $60M fixed-payment licence booked $15M in Q2) and a $10.9M tax benefit from option exercises. Recurring Q2 EPS is about $0.47. Q3 guidance rose from ~10% to >30% sequential in September on VPD licence royalties, and there are now four licensees. Consensus is FY26 $632M revenue / $3.91 EPS and FY27 $969M / $6.32. At $305.61 the stock trades at 48x next-year EPS against an 11-peer median of 27.6x. Separating one-offs from recurring product and royalty earnings and capitalising them inside the peer range gives a fair value of about $176 (P/E SOTP $170, DCF $181). Base rates (my lane): VICR has had three prior re-ratings, in 2018, 2021 and 2023, each retracing 51-68% within roughly 12 months of the peak. The extreme-performer literature finds no positive market-adjusted drift after 5x moves. The stock has already shown it can halve within this cycle: -54% from June to September 2026. Against that, this cycle has a real earnings and royalty base (backlog +145% y/y) and a live licensing option, so I do not put the median at fair value. I use a 3-scenario lognormal mixture: bear $140 (35%), base $275 (42%), bull $500 (23%), each with a 30-40% spread. That gives a median of about $259, a mean of about $280, P(>=spot) of about 38% and P(>=$535) of about 10%. Macro input: Kalshi's 2027 US recession market is at 21% (yes ask $0.21, ~603k contracts traded, 2026-10-06). Sell-side targets ($387-394) and option-implied data were not used. Research was limited: Twelve Data statistics and estimates and Alpha Vantage were unavailable (plan or rate limits), sec.gov refused direct downloads (filings were read via WebFetch), and some aggregator pages were blocked.
